diagnosticHistory.observation: Single-frame WebGPU canvas screenshot returned only the page background while the locked offscreen RGBA32F hash remained correct.
A continuous Three.js presentation loop did not change the blank WebGPU screenshot result; the provisional gate failed because it still required a measurable WebGPU screenshot.

fixture.source: exact R55 stepwise float32 premultiplied source-over output
fixture.readback: Playwright PNG screenshot of the CSS canvas rectangle while continuous presentation is active

Observation: Both software backends reproduced the locked R55 premultiplied float source exactly in an offscreen RGBA32F NoColorSpace target.
WebGL screenshots distinguished Linear-sRGB from sRGB output and matched the analytic black-background result exactly for both output spaces.

WebGL white-background screenshots differed from the analytic rounded byte result by at most one code; transparent PNG RGB differed by at most three codes for Linear-sRGB and four for sRGB while alpha matched.
Headless WebGPU screenshots returned only the requested page background in all six cases, both before and after a continuous presentation-loop control.
Candidate: Transparent PNG RGB residuals are consistent with quantized premultiplied-canvas to straight-PNG conversion, but the exact browser pipeline cause was not independently isolated.
Use opaque black and white background captures alongside transparent PNG when validating presentation; a transparent PNG alone mixes transfer, alpha unpremultiplication and screenshot behavior.
statusLedger.CurrentBestView: On the locked software WebGL/Chromium path, Three.js r186 NoToneMapping presentation follows the declared Linear-sRGB or sRGB transfer and premultiplied-alpha background composition within the observed fixture envelopes. The same claim cannot be extended to the WebGPU canvas because this headless screenshot path exposed no surface pixels despite exact offscreen output.
